main_issue: Whether alcohol will be served at the housewarming given Agent D's Hindu parents are attending and object to alcohol in the home, versus A and B's need for drinks.

A-B.evidence: A (15) says she already bought the drinks; B (16) says it is a problem for him too as he told colleagues there would be drinks. Both want drinks, but they never address each other.

A-C.evidence: C (19) acknowledges A is out of pocket and that a total ban doesn't work for her, but C stays a mediator without endorsing A's plan.

A-D.evidence: D proposes no alcohol (14); A replies she already bought it and can't return it (15). D still rejects the delay idea (18).

B-C.evidence: C (17) offers a dry period then drinks after, which addresses B's concern, and C (19) says a ban doesn't work for B, but C does not fully side with B.

B-D.evidence: D wants no alcohol (14) and B says the drinks are needed for his manager and colleagues (16). They never speak to each other.

C-D.evidence: C is sympathetic and offers moving the drinks out (11) or a dry period (17). D rejects both as awkward (12, 18), and C says D's concern matters but all four need a solution (19).
